L78@P3: MESSAGE FROM THE LIBRARIAN
L79@P3: Libraries today have the singular role of bringing information to our patrons (users), in
L80@P3: the most acceptable way that these patrons can make use of. Today, librarians have
L81@P3: closely followed Shannon principle in communication, though a mathematical theory, to
L82@P3: provide contemporary services to their clientele. Not only does the library only house
L83@P3: books; but also provides information, in various formats and through various means.
L84@P3: Welcome to the University of Eastern Africa Baraton Library (UEAB) where we pride in
L85@P3: making a difference in our academic studies. At UEAB Library we provide you with a
L86@P3: modern-day approach to information services.
L87@P3: Here you will be in a community of academicians who have long trusted our productivity
L88@P3: for research. Services provided by the library are geared towards making your stay at
L89@P3: UEAB a very comfortable one; you will be able to meet the challenges of academic
L90@P3: research with ease as you tap from the fountain of knowledge that provides you with the
L91@P3: opportunities to not only learn but also develop skills for research.
L92@P3: One of the tools the library uses is social media in connecting with our patrons. Whatever
L93@P3: platform you may be comfortable with, the Library will be more than pleased to meet you
L94@P3: there with the assistance you need. Countless individuals have joined our WhatsApp
L95@P3: platforms for Faculty and Staff, Students, Alumni, Friends of the Library and even Juvenile
L96@P3: users. Other social media tools are Facebook, YouTube, the various Google Services and
L97@P3: many more. Contact us anytime and we will be more than glad to help you.
L98@P3: Our simple philosophy is that we can be restored to our Maker through quality education
L99@P3: that nurtures the whole being of an individual. Our restoration is key to unleashing our
L100@P3: God-Given potential to positively affect this world today. Therefore, we strive for
L101@P3: excellence under the direction of God Himself to make learners have a lifelong experience
L102@P3: of reflecting Jesus Christ.
L103@P3: The Library is at your service both to learn and to grow in knowledge. We will be happy
L104@P3: to partner with you in your stay here at UEAB. Please visit the relevant sections of our
L105@P3: website to know more about making the most of UEAB Library.
L106@P3-4: Be Blessed Always.UEAB Library Handbook
L107@P4: 5
L108@P4: INTRODUCTION
L109@P4: The library is maintained primarily for the use by the University of Eastern Africa, Baraton
L110@P4: students, faculty, and staff. Their spouses and children may also use the Library.
L111@P4: Educators, researchers, and pastors may apply for a library card which will entitle them
L112@P4: to use the library but not to check out materials. Presently the Library has access to
L113@P4: approximately 70,000 volumes of books, subscribes to print and online periodical titles,
L114@P4: and electronic databases. It also has access to thousands monographs and millions journal
L115@P4: titles through subscriptions to online databases and e-books. These information
L116@P4: resources support certificate, diploma, undergraduate and postgraduate programs in all
L117@P4: the disciplines offered at UEAB.
L118@P4: VISION
L119@P4: To be a leading center of excellence in promoting teaching, learning and research
L120@P4: activities of the University
L121@P4: MISSION
L122@P4: UEAB library promotes and advances quality integrated, innovative and user-friendly
L123@P4: library services to enhance teaching, learning and research activities by providing an
L124@P4: environment that blends academic, spiritual and social spaces
L125@P4: OBJECTIVES
L126@P4: The objectives of UEAB library are:
L127@P4:  To provide collections that evolve with the changing information environment
L128@P4: and align with University curricular and research needs.
L129@P4:  To provide a conducive environment for all users.
L130@P4:  Engage in current and appropriate assessment of services, outreach, collections
L131@P4: and workflows.
L132@P4:  Utilize analytic tools associated with the library services platform to improve
L133@P4-5: library services and operations.UEAB Library Handbook
L134@P5: 6
L135@P5: SECTION ONE: GENERAL LIBRARY PROCEDURES
L136@P5: LIBRARY HOURS
L137@P5: Sunday-Thursday 7:00 am-5:30 pm; 7:00 pm-10:30 pm
L138@P5: Friday 7:00 am-2:00 pm
L139@P5: Saturday 7:30 pm-10:30 pm
L140@P5: Public Holidays: The Library will operate usual opening hours and remain closed
L141@P5: when the University is not in session.
L142@P5: National Holidays: 2:00 pm-5:30 pm; 7:00 pm-10:30 pm
L143@P5: LIBRARY MEMBERSHIP
L144@P5: 1. Students
L145@P5: a. Students form the bulk of the Library patrons. Students are automatic
L146@P5: users or the library, after they are duly registered as students of the
L147@P5: university. Undergraduate Students may borrow up to six (6) books
L148@P5: from the Library’s main stacks. Books from the mains stack can be
L149@P5: borrowed for up to two (2) weeks, after which failure to return them
L150@P5: will attract a fine.
L151@P5: b. Postgraduate students are eligible to borrow up to ten (10) materials
L152@P5: at a time for a period of one month.
L153@P5: 2. Workers
L154@P5: The Faculty and Staff of the university are our next group of patrons.
L155@P5: Faculty are eligible to borrow a maximum of 18 materials for a period
L156@P5: of three months. Staff on the other hand are eligible to borrow a
L157@P5: maximum of 4 materials. Where a staff serves as a student
L158@P5: concurrently, the student status shall be applied.
L159@P5: 3. Children of Workers
L160@P5: Juveniles of Faculty and Staff, upon recommendations from their
L161@P5: parents could have borrowing privileges. Each individual is issued with
L162@P5: a borrower’s ID and could check out four (4) materials at a time. Loan
L163@P5: period is the same as for undergraduate students.
L164@P5: 4. Community Members
L165@P5: The community members of Baraton and its environment are the
L166@P5: Library’s next set of patrons. Community members who wish to use
L167@P5: the Library are required to obtain application forms from the
L168@P5: Information Desk, which should be filled and returned either via the
L169@P5-6: library email or to the Information Desk.UEAB Library Handbook
L170@P6: 7
L171@P6: SECURITY (ENTRANCE AND EXIT)
L172@P6: 1. Entering the Library
L173@P6: a. Present your valid university ID card, before you are allowed to enter
L174@P6: the library. Entry will be denied to individuals who do not present a
L175@P6: valid university ID Card.
L176@P6: b. Leave your bag or any other belongings you bring to the library, at the
L177@P6: luggage section. It is advisable you take out your valuables from your
L178@P6: bag before handing it over for keeping while you are in the library as
L179@P6: the library shall not be held responsible for the loss of any item
L180@P6: reported missing from bags kept at the library; patrons leave their bags
L181@P6: at their own risk at the luggage section of the library.
L182@P6: 2. Exiting the Library
L183@P6: a. Depending on the time and circumstances you may find the luggage
L184@P6: section either within the library or without. In the event the luggage
L185@P6: section is within the library, you will be required to hand over your bag
L186@P6: for inspection (after taking it back from the luggage section), by the
L187@P6: Library Exit Security Desk. Bags deposited at the luggage section
L188@P6: outside the library are not required to be inspected before the owners
L189@P6: take them away.
L190@P6: b. Bags left unattended to (after Library hours) in the library will be
L191@P6: confiscated. Owners will have to identify and pay a fee for the return
L192@P6: of their bags.
L193@P6: THE INFORMATION DESK
L194@P6: Information seeking
L195@P6: The Library Information Desk attends to all queries from library patrons. It is important
L196@P6: therefore to stop over at the desk and make any inquiry you may need.
L197@P6: 1. LOST/DAMAGED OR STOLEN ID CARDS
L198@P6: Lost or stolen ID cards must be reported immediately to the Users’ Services Librarian. A
L199@P6: replacement is issued at a cost at the Registry department.
L200@P6: Before leaving the institution, each borrower must return all materials on loan to him/her
L201@P6: from the Library and clear accordingly.
L202@P6: All messages from the Library are sent via email. So, ensure that you indicate your email
L203@P6-7: address on the ID card registration form.UEAB Library Handbook
L204@P7: 8
L205@P7: SECTION TWO: SECTIONS OF THE LIBRARY
L206@P7: 1. THE CIRCULATION AREA
L207@P7: This is the big wooden counter that users encounter as they enter the Library. Materials
L208@P7: are signed out and returned at the counter. Reserved materials are also borrowed at the
L209@P7: Counter.
L210@P7: 2. REFERENCE ROOM
L211@P7: The Reference Room is located in the room just behind the Circulation Desk. Materials in
L212@P7: this room are under “close access". They are to be accessed only in the room. They are
L213@P7: not to be taken out and cannot be checked out of the Library.
L214@P7: 3. PERIODICALS ROOM
L215@P7: The Periodicals Room is arranged into three sections: The bound periodicals section is on
L216@P7: the extreme left. The current periodicals are in the center of the room. They are arranged
L217@P7: on shelves according to their subject areas. The periodicals librarian's office houses
L218@P7: periodicals yet to be bound.
L219@P7: All periodicals are to be used within the Periodicals Room. They are not checked out of
L220@P7: the Library.
L221@P7: 4. WORLD BANK PUBLICATIONS
L222@P7: This is an open access collection. The collection is a prime source of information and
L223@P7: data on economic and social development in more than 150 countries. The Library is a
L224@P7: depository of the World Bank publications. Current World Bank publications can be
L225@P7: accessed at: http://ebrary.worldbank.org
L226@P7: 5. OVERSIZE MATERIALS
L227@P7: These are shelved near the end of the Main Stack. They include circulation books,
L228@P7: reference books and bound periodicals that are designated "oversize".
L229@P7: 6. VERTICAL FILE MATERIALS
L230@P7: They are designated "VF" and are kept in file cabinets in the Periodicals Room. These files
L231@P7: contain pamphlets and other thin items, such as clippings, maps and pictures. There is
L232@P7: also a collection of overhead transparencies on biblical topics, designated "Tra".
L233@P7: Generally vertical file materials are for use within the Library, but in some cases, these
L234@P7: items may be taken out for short periods by arrangement with the Librarian.
L235@P7: 7. SPECIAL COLLECTION
L236@P7: It is adjacent to the Information Desk, as you enter the library, and next to your immediate
L237@P7: left as you take the staircase to the Main Stack. It comprises the following: -
L238@P7: ● Government Publications
L239@P7-8: They are under close access, hence cannot be checked out.UEAB Library Handbook
L240@P8: 9
L241@P8: ● Baraton Collection
L242@P8: This is a collection of theses, dissertations, articles and works published by the faculty,
L243@P8: staff and students of this institution. Again, materials in this category cannot be checked
L244@P8: out of the Library.
L245@P8: ● Africana Collection
L246@P8: These are publications about Africa and people of African origin. Resources in this section
L247@P8: are under close access.
L248@P8: ● Multimedia Collection
L249@P8: These materials are classified and arranged in a small room. Audio materials are used
L250@P8: within the Library. Films, slides, and video are loaned out for a period of 4 days.
L251@P8: ● The Microfiche collection
L252@P8: This is for use within its section in the Special Collection unit.
L253@P8: 8. STUDY ROOMS
L254@P8: There are three study rooms on the ground floor and a small one in the Special Collection
L255@P8: unit for post-graduate students. At the upper floor of the library, students may use the
L256@P8: Main Stack, Reference room and a room designated ‘Study Room’.
L257@P8: 9. DISCUSSION ROOM
L258@P8: Patrons who would like to engage in discussions can make use of our discussion room
L259@P8: located on the ground floor next to the undergraduate Online Research Centre (ORC).
L260@P8: This area is meant for academic discussions and patrons are thus cautioned to keep to
L261@P8: that.
L262@P8: 10. POSTGRADUATES AND UNDERGRADUATES ONLINE RESEARCH CENTRE
L263@P8: There are two rooms reserved for a variety of online learning activities, research, writing,
L264@P8: technology skills development and personal study. The spaces are described thus:
L265@P8: ● One large room consisting of 30 networked computers and another room with
L266@P8: 2 networked computers respectively. The network is for legitimate academic
L267@P8: purposes only. Social emailing, chatting, and game playing are not permitted
L268@P8: and could result in temporary loss of computing privileges. Printing from the
L269@P8: network is available.
L270@P8: ● There are two rooms on the first floor next to the main stack reserved for
L271@P8: postgraduate personal study. The rooms are internet enabled and these
L272@P8-9: students can carry out their research work.UEAB Library Handbook

L274@P9: SECTION THREE: RESOURCES AND SERVICES
L275@P9: ORGANIZATION OF LIBRARY RESOURCES
L276@P9: The classification system used for arranging books and bound periodicals on the shelves
L277@P9: is the Library of Congress System. The first part of each classification number consists of
L278@P9: one or more letters designating the general subject area. The next part is the number
L279@P9: designating a narrower part of the subject. Further parts consist of a mixture of letters
L280@P9: and numbers, sometimes including the date of publication. You will find the number at
L281@P9: the bottom of the catalog in KOHA (OPAC). Above it, you may find an abbreviation or a
L282@P9: word indicating the item is in a specific collection, such as "Ref" for Reference books,
L283@P9: “Per” for Periodicals. When you copy the number (usually referred to as the call number),
L284@P9: be sure to copy the entire line of the number.

L313@P9: FINDING A BOOK
L314@P9: The library is automated using KOHA Library management system. For an effective use of
L315@P9: library resources therefore, patrons need to get acquainted with the arrangement of
L316@P9: resources as well as the online public access catalog (OPAC) that points to places on the
L317@P9: shelves where materials can be found. The catalogue can be accessed online from
L318@P9: anywhere at any time as long as there is Internet connectivity.
L319@P9: USING OPAC
L320@P9: Go to the Library: http://opac.ueab.ac.ke
L321@P9: Create your account by clicking “My Account”
L322@P9: LOGGING INTO YOUR ACCOUNT
L323@P9-10: ● Enter the web address- http://opac.ueab.ac.keUEAB Library Handbook
L324@P10: 11
L325@P10: ● Click “Log in to your Account” located top right of your screen.
L326@P10: ● Enter your library ID number
L327@P10: ● Enter your ID number again and add a small (s) at the end as your PIN, you are
L328@P10: advised to change this PIN to something that you can easily remember. This can
L329@P10: be done after logging in.
L330@P10: While logged in, you can view your basic account information: items borrowed, due
L331@P10: dates, your borrowing history, and your fines. Once you can operate your account, you
L332@P10: will be able to do the following:
L333@P10: ● save searches to your account;
L334@P10: ● make a list;
L335@P10: ● print your list, or export your list as a bibliography;
L336@P10: ● place a request (hold) on a title; and
L337@P10: ● Or renew (Renewals) some of the items on your list that are about to expire.
L338@P10: HOW TO SEARCH FOR MATERIALS
L339@P10: From this site, http://opac.ueab.ac.ke/cgi-bin/koha/opac-user.pl
L340@P10: you can search the catalogue by:
L341@P10: ● Basic Search
L342@P10: ● Advanced Search
L343@P10: Basic Search Search by subject, title, author, call number, series, ISBN,
L344@P10: ISSN.
L345@P10: Advanced Search Search by keywords, item type, publication date range,
L346@P10: language using complex queries to return highly focused
L347@P10: results
L348@P10: Use ‘Exactly March’ or ‘Begins With’ button to further
L349@P10: refine search criteria.
L350@P10: Fiction Search for general and subject related fiction by clicking
L351@P10: the ‘Browse Genre’ button.
L352@P10: New Arrivals Click on ‘New Titles’ to the left of the screen to browse new
L353@P10: arrivals
L354@P10: Set Limits Limit searches by Collection, Format, Language, Place and
L355@P10: Search Branch. You can also limit by Dates, Available Items
L356@P10: Only, or change the number of results displayed on each
L357@P10: page.
L358@P10: Single click on the Search button to open up the database.
L359@P10: To execute a SUBJECT search, type your topic in the dialog box and press <enter> or click
L360@P10: the search button.
L361@P10-11: In this example, the subject Information technology was entered.UEAB Library Handbook
L362@P11: 12
L363@P11: Search Examples
L364@P11: Keyword Search Combine search terms with: AND OR BUT; e.g. Nutrition and
L365@P11: Diseases
L366@P11: Use quotes to search phrases: “Second language learning”
L367@P11: Use (?) to truncate: employ? = employee, employment,
L368@P11: employed
L369@P11: Subject Browse Search by any subject, e.g. History
L370@P11: HOW TO LOCATE LIBRARY MATERIALS
L371@P11: Each material is given a call number consisting of a combination of letters and numbers.
L372@P11: The call number is located on the spine of the book and is the book's address. In the
L373@P11: Library of Congress Classification System, a typical call number has three parts: The first
L374@P11: part identifies the book by broad subject discipline; the second part represents a
L375@P11: subcategory of the discipline, and the third part identifies the author.
L376@P11: For instance, using the call number HD 57.7. P57 2015, the H represents the broad
L377@P11: discipline of social science, while HD represents industries, land use and labor, a branch
L378@P11-12: of social science. Point 7 (.7) signifies a further breakdown in this particular branch of UEAB Library Handbook
L379@P12: 13
L380@P12: social science. P57 identifies the author's last name and 2015 states the year of
L381@P12: publication.
L382@P12: Most books in the collection stand together on shelves referred to as the MAIN STACKS.
L383@P12: If the material belongs in the Main Stacks, the book will have a label on the spine that
L384@P12: reads:
L385@P12: HD
L386@P12: 57.7

L389@P12: Some books stand in special areas like REFERENCE, and OVERSIZE. Books that are not in
L390@P12: the MAIN STACKS carry their special collection codes on their spine labels. For example:

L21: ## About KNLS
L22: Kenya National Library Service (KNLS) is a state corporation with a mandate to promote, establish, equip, manage, maintain, and develop the National Library of Kenya; and collect, preserve, make available and promote the national documentary heritage for both present and future generations.
L23: Two of the key features of KNLS is that it is the national bibliographic agency, thus ensuring production of a comprehensive annual Kenya National Bibliography; and also, the International Standard Book (ISBN) agency that manages the issuance of ISBNs to all Kenyan Publishers and Authors. KNLS has its headquarters at Maktaba Kuu Building, with two branches at Buruburu and Nakuru.
